aggressive_definition: Aggressive prostate cancer and advanced-stage prostate cancer were analyzed as incident subtypes, but the abstract does not report their defining criteria.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.
study_design: Pooled individual-participant-data analysis of matched case-control sets from 15 prospective studies.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.
reason: The abstract reports associations with overall incident prostate cancer and separately reports aggressive incident prostate cancer estimates for lycopene and α-tocopherol.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: the OR for aggressive disease for the highest compared with the lowest fifth of lycopene was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.46, 0.91; P-trend = 0.032).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported lycopene estimate explicitly concerns aggressive prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For α-tocopherol, the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78, 0.94; P-trend < 0.001), with significant heterogeneity by stage of disease; the OR for aggressive prostate cancer was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.59, 0.92; P-trend = 0.001).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row's OR of 0.86 is the overall prostate cancer estimate; the separate aggressive estimate is 0.74.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For retinol, the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth was 1.13 (95% CI: 1.04, 1.22; P-trend = 0.015).
estimate_classifications.reason: The retinol estimate is presented as an overall prostate cancer association, not as an aggressive-disease estimate.
